record_title: Two-prime rigidity for the multiplier-four iterate of the unitary divisor sum
scientific_context: For odd prime p, any solution sigma*^2(2^a p^b)=4·2^a p^b must have p=3 and b even; in the square-exponent slice b=2 the unique solution is 18=2·3^2.
limitations: The remaining two-prime-support family 2^a 3^(2m) with m>=2 is not classified, and no result is claimed for three or more distinct prime factors. Originality is to the best of our knowledge; the main residual risk is equivalent coverage under alternate (m,k)-perfect terminology. The bounded verification supports but does not replace the proof, and no formal proof-assistant verification or independent audit is asserted.

artifact_inventory.description: Standalone exact-integer direct check of the iterated unitary divisor-sum equation on a bounded two-prime-power grid.
